narrative:
Second run, in another lifetime, with the eighth set's windows. 32 steps recorded (wire-time spin step excluded, one snapshot taken by the poll window). 24 of 32 steps contained an interrupt. All snapshots 0xff9e; no fault. Image verdict: pass against 1,268 permille.

Access costs (second run; first run in parentheses; per iteration; sub-window range):
| Window | Average | Sub-windows |
| CNTR read with DSB SY before and after | 418.5 ns (418.8) | 416.7 to 420.6 |
| Plain CNTR read, value discarded | 377.9 (377.9) | 376.3 to 378.9 |
| Plain CNTR read, address-dependent | 379.1 (378.7) | 377.6 to 380.2 |
| Adapter time read | 144.4 (143.6) | 141.9 to 151.0 |
| Adapter register read | 462.2 (462.4) | 460.9 to 470.1 |
| Task check | 77.0 (76.5) | 75.5 to 83.3 |
| Trace observer | 42.5 (43.5) | 40.4 to 52.1 |
| Plain XADDR write, one DSB SY per 32 | 200.7; 197.6 less the empty window | 186.2 to 204.4 |
| Empty window, one DSB SY per 32 | 3.1 ns; 99 ns per sub-window | 2 to 5 ticks per sub-window |
| Service loop between polls | 274.6 | 272.1 to 286.5 |
| Whole provider poll with the flag clear | 1,245.4; 1,175.8 less its stamp pair | 1,225.3 to 1,263.0 |
| Stamp pair of a poll sample | 69.7 | 69.0 to 70.3 |

The 2,040 S_TWI0 writes inside the snapshots took 17,618 ticks, 359.9 ns on average (358.1 ns in the first run), from 8 ticks (333 ns) to 10 ticks (417 ns). The poll window took its 256 samples from the 398 polls of one snapshot. After the XADDR write window, XADDR, ADDR, CNTR, STAT and LCR read the same values as before: XADDR 0x0, CNTR 0x40, STAT 0xf8, LCR 0x3a. The wire-time spin read CNTR 40 times in 554 ticks, 577 ns per iteration; each iteration is an adapter read without the observer (462 ns at idle), a raw counter stamp (about 35 ns, half the stamp pair) and the spin's own record keeping. The window does not separate the record keeping, so it bounds a CNTR read while a byte is on the wire at about 80 ns above the idle read and does not show whether it costs more.

How the windows divide the costs:
- Reads: the DSB SY pair adds 41 ns to a read. Issue throughput and latency agree, so a plain read waits for its completion either way.
- Writes: a plain write costs 198 ns when 32 run back to back before one DSB SY. The adapter's write with a DSB SY pair costs about 325 ns in the transfers (the 359.9 ns bracket less one counter read, half the stamp pair). Of the 325 ns, about 44 ns are the adapter's checks (its read less the fenced read) and about 20 ns the leading DSB SY, leaving about 261 ns from the store to its completion. One completed write therefore takes 198 to 261 ns.
- Polls: the whole flag-clear poll, 1,176 ns, holds the task check (77 ns), the time read (144 ns), the flag read with its observer call (505 ns) and 449 ns of other provider software (entry, try-lock, deadline and revocation checks, phase dispatch, release).
- Service loop: its time read takes 144 ns of the 275 ns, and the two work queries the other 131 ns.

conditions.window: completing-poll window: a counter stamp at the entry of every a733_pmic_poll(); a poll that completes a bus phase ends its span at the stamp after its first phase-start CNTR write returns

conclusion: Completing polls explain about 12 us of the 45 us gap between the modeled 739 us and the second run; about 38 us is step work outside completing polls that no window times yet. The completing-poll window itself costs about 12 us per step, so it is a diagnostic option and off in the default image.
narrative:
Third run, with the completing-poll window; 32 steps recorded, wire-time spin step excluded. Steps after the first 795 to 805 us. All snapshots 0xff9e; no fault. Image verdict: pass against 1,268 permille (3 permille, about 2 us, below the limit).

Completing-poll spans (each from the stamp at the poll entry to the return of its phase-start CNTR write):
| Kind | Spans | Mean measured | Model, measured costs and stamp | Measured less model |
| Byte (DATA then CNTR) | 575 | 3.10 us | 2.72 | 0.38 |
| Receive (CNTR alone) | 192 | 2.52 | 2.32 | 0.20 |
| Repeated START | 192 | 2.49 | 2.32 | 0.17 |
| START after a STOP wait | 160 | 2.56 | 2.32 | 0.25 |
| STOP, after the DATA read | 192 | 3.29 | 2.97 | 0.32 |
The model column charges the second run's measured costs plus the window's own stamp, 87 ns, by which the whole flag-clear poll grew between the second and third runs (1,175.8 ns to 1,262.9 ns). The counts are those of 32 recorded steps: 18 byte phases, 6 receives, 6 repeated STARTs, 5 STARTs after a STOP wait and 6 STOPs per snapshot, less one byte. The first START of a request follows admission and completes no phase, so it is not a span.

The difference grows with the accesses a poll makes after its first read: 0.17 to 0.25 us for the polls with two reads and one write, 0.32 us with a third read, and 0.38 us with a second write. Inside a poll each fenced access therefore costs more than in the isolated windows, where no provider-state stores precede the leading DSB SY, and each write carries the wrapper's second counter stamp, atomic exchange and observer call. The flag-clear poll, with one read and no write, holds none of that difference.

Per step, the spans total 118.2 us against the model's 106.2 us with the stamp. With the poll cost set to 919 ns (model span total matched at this run's 505 ns per read and 395 ns per write) the model gives 758 us, 38 us below the run's 796 us median. The completing polls account for about 12 us of the per-step difference between model and board; about 38 us lies in step work other than completing polls: the admission with its two lock waits, the first START, the final STOP's line-control read and the publication that releases the I2C mutex. No window times that work.

Window cost: the stamp at every poll entry adds 87 ns to each phase's serial work. The median, 796.4 us (1,265 permille), is 12.5 us above the second run's and 10 us above the 786 to 787 us predicted with 2 to 3 us for the window; the 87 ns moves most phases across a whole microsecond, so the window costs about 12 us per step although its stamps spend about 3.6 us. With the window present the median lies within 3 to 6 permille of the 1,268 permille limit; 2 of 32 steps exceeded it (the second run had 1). The default bundle 6 image therefore omits the window (checks/board-bundles-apps.py --complete-window builds it in for diagnosis; the default image's TWI_COMPLETE lines print window=0 with empty records). The limit stays at 1,268 permille because it describes the provider under bundle 6's standing instrumentation; raising it to absorb a diagnostic window would loosen it for every later run without a change in the provider. The windows give no authority for a PMIC rail write.

narrative:
Fourth run. Third run with DSB SY pairs versus fourth run with plain DATA:
| Metric | Third run | Fourth run |
| Median step | 796.4 us (19,114.5 ticks), 1,265 permille | 794.6 us (19,070 ticks), 1,262 permille |
| Steps after the first | 794.5 to 804.6 us | 793.5 to 801.4 us |
| Steps above 1,268 permille | 2 of 32 | 2 of 32 |
| First step | 823.6 us, limit 838.8 us | 819.3 us, limit 838.8 us |
| Adapter read window | 461.1 ns | 421.4 ns |
| Write bracket in the transfers | 351.2 ns | 277.7 ns |
| Snapshots; TWI_WRITE lines | All 0xff9e; XADDR unchanged | The same values |

Completing-poll spans (third run, fourth run, saving per poll, saving per step): byte 3.10, 2.76, 0.33, 6.0 us; receive 2.52, 2.43, 0.08, 0.5; repeated START 2.49, 2.44, 0.05, 0.3; START after a STOP wait 2.56, 2.53, 0.03, 0.2; STOP 3.29, 3.21, 0.08, 0.5. Total saving 7.4 us per step.

A byte's completing poll (two reads, two writes) saved 0.33 us; the isolated windows predicted 0.19 to 0.21 us. The 0.12 to 0.15 us beyond that fits the leading DSB SY of each fenced access waiting for the poll's own provider-state stores, which the windows do not make.

The median fell by 1.9 us (3 permille), against the 8 us the model predicted and the 7.4 us that the completing polls saved. Each phase costs its spin plus the whole microseconds its serial work spans. With DSB SY pairs a byte phase's serial work is about 3.3 us (its 3.10 us completing poll plus about 0.2 us before the poll and after its write); with plain DATA it is about 3.0 us, still at or just above 3 us in most byte phases, so few phases lost a whole microsecond. The model with its poll cost matched to each run's span total gives 758 us and 748 us, a 10 us difference, because its phases sit at other fractions of a microsecond.

For the 110% route: a per-phase saving shortens the step only in whole microseconds per phase. Another 0.1 to 0.2 us per byte phase would lower the 18 byte phases of a snapshot by 1 us each, about 18 us, and a saving that leaves a phase above its boundary gives nothing. Reaching 693 us from the fourth run's 795 us, or about 783 us without the window, needs about 90 us: about 2 us from each of the 42 phases, beyond what the register accesses leave, or the per-transaction turnaround of the S_TWI0 packet engine, together with the about 38 us of step work outside the completing polls. The barrier placement does not change that route.

hypothesis: Set a provisional empirical acceptance bound for the bundle 6 snapshot step from the first changed-provider run.
prediction: The first run median of 779.292 us plus 20 us margin gives a limit near 799 us, 1,268 permille of the nominal wire time.

conditions.bundle: bundle 6 at 400 kHz, CPU-L 494 MHz, one service core, trace observer and write stamps enabled
conditions.evaluator: rounds ratios up from counter ticks; compares the first step with the counter 125/3 ns tick directly; upper distribution bin is also 1,268 permille
conditions.byte_rule: wire time per step uses the measured byte, the lower bracket of the wire-time spin when it exceeds nine bit times, at most 110% of nine bit times

conclusion: The 1,268-permille median limit plus a 40 us first-step allowance is a provisional empirical bound that two runs have passed; it is not derived from a model.
narrative:
Derivation. The first run's median is 18,703 counter ticks, 779.292 us, 123.7% of wire time. Its image printed 1,236 permille because its evaluator rounded down; the revised evaluator prints 1,237. Adding 20 us and rounding down to a whole permille gives the 1,268-permille limit (798.840 us at nominal wire time), about 19.55 us above that median. The first-step allowance adds 40 us (838.840 us at nominal wire time, 30 us above the first run's observed first step of 809 us). The limit is an empirical acceptance limit set from the first run; no model or cost measurement derives it, and it is not a worst-case bound. It holds only under the bundle conditions above; changed clock rates, instrumentation or bus timing need a new assessment. The model is not used to claim an independently measured margin.

Byte rule. A measured byte that is missing or above 110% of nine bit times fails the bound and the raw stamps are printed. It fails rather than being capped at 110%: the run measures the provider's cost per step against the wire time that the divisor sets, and a byte that much longer means the bus ran slower (clock stretching or a wrong divisor). A capped wire time would charge that bus time to the provider, so such a run needs a bus diagnosis before any bound is set from it. A spin with fewer than two reads has no read with the flag clear and therefore no lower bracket; bundle 6 then takes nine bit times, as for a missing sample, and its WIRE line shows reads=1; the model treats that sample as missing. Unlike a missing sample it does not fail the bound, because with nine bit times the verdict can only be stricter. The service spins 23 us for a 22.5 us byte and spin ends fall on whole microseconds, so a step changes in whole microseconds per phase.

Re-spins are reported per step and in the summary and do not gate the run: the service model gives no re-spin at a 23 us byte and 18 to 24 per snapshot at 24 us. Each re-spin costs a quarter bit time and one poll, about 1.5 us. Neither run of the changed provider that applied the bound had one.

Applications. The second run applied the limit in another lifetime and passed (median 1,243 permille, first step 807 us against 840 us). The fifth and sixth prepared sets' preserved images and runbooks retain their original 1,550-permille limit. Production images omit the instrumentation (trace observer, write stamps) and their step times were not measured. The trace evaluator, distribution labels, host fixtures, controlled-outcome helper and bundle preparation row use 1,268 permille.

hypothesis: The host model of the power service, charged with the measured access costs, reproduces the board snapshot step.
prediction: At 505 ns per read, 403 ns per write, 145 ns per time read and 527 ns per poll the model gives a 739 us snapshot and a 950 us selector write in one step.

conditions.model: checks/power-domains-service.c --board-costs; flags set at the write completion time in ns plus the phase wire time; 400 kHz
conditions.costs: 505 ns per read (adapter read plus observer), 403 ns per write (write bracket plus observer), 145 ns per time read, 527 ns per poll (task check plus the 449 ns remainder)

conclusion: The model with measured component costs under-predicts the board median by 40 to 45 us; about 12 us is completing-poll cost (record pmic-access-bb6-run3-complete-window) and about 38 us is unmeasured step work. 110% of wire time is not reachable by register-access savings alone; it needs the packet engine or fewer serial accesses.
narrative:
Model results. At the measured costs the model gives a 739 us snapshot (117% of the 630 us bit-time wire time) and a 950 us selector write in one step. The snapshot is 45 us below the second run's median and 40 us below the first run's. Charging the task check alone as the poll cost gives 731 us, so the whole poll accounts for 8 us of the difference. It replaces the 299 ns per-poll remainder of an earlier fit, which also charged 1,026 ns per write, with a measured 449 ns. It does not explain the remaining 45 us.

Step times move in whole microseconds per phase. The provider stores phase_at in whole microseconds, the service spins until phase_at plus the rounded-up phase time, and the spin ends at the first time read at or after that whole microsecond. The next spin starts from the time read after the next phase-start write. Each phase therefore costs its spin (23 us for a byte, 5 us for a condition) plus the whole microseconds spanned by its serial work, which runs from the end of the spin through the work query, the poll entry, the flag and status reads and the phase-start writes to that time read. In the model at the measured costs that work spans 2 us in each of the 42 phases. A poll cost of 1,500 ns, about 970 ns per phase more than the measured costs, brings the model to 783 us, within 1 us of the board's median, and splits the selector write into two steps with one tick wait. The board therefore spends about 41 us per step on work the model does not charge. Candidates: the two further phase passes, revocation loads and time-read bookkeeping of a completing poll, which a flag-clear poll does once; the write wrapper's second counter stamp, atomic exchange and observer call, about 70 ns per write outside the bracket; DSB SY waiting for the provider-state stores that precede each access inside a poll, which the isolated windows do not make; per-step work outside the phases, such as the admission's two lock waits.

110% is not reachable by the register accesses of this design. The target is 693 us for a snapshot. With every software cost set to zero, the model charges only the register accesses and a 35 ns counter read per time read, and gives 712 us (113%) with a DSB SY pair around each access (419 ns per read, 281 ns per write) and 694 us (110.2%) with the plain-DATA placement (378 ns per read, 235 ns per write). Each phase of a snapshot spins its rounded wire time, 23 us for a byte and 5 us for a condition, which already makes 642 us of the 693 us. The 51 us that remain cover 42 phases, about 1.2 us each. The serial register accesses of a phase that writes DATA and CNTR take about 1.2 us with the lighter placement (two plain reads, a plain write and a completed write) and 1.4 us with DSB SY pairs. Any route to 110% needs fewer serial register accesses per snapshot. The S_TWI0 packet engine (the TWI_DRV registers from +0x200, which startup requires disabled) sequences the conditions and bytes of a transaction in hardware and would leave one software turnaround per transaction instead of one per phase, six per snapshot instead of 42; it is not designed or qualified. Reading the status register alone to detect completion removes one read per phase (up to about 16 us per snapshot) but not enough to reach 110% at the present software cost.

Selector write: at the poll cost that reproduces the board's snapshot median the model splits a DCDC3 selector write into two steps with one tick wait; the acceptance bound stays at most two steps with one tick wait, not measured on the board. The service checks its 1 ms spin budget between polls, so a final poll can finish slightly later than 1 ms.

narrative:
Budget rows, base versus head:

The 400 kHz 110% assertion at 200 ns per access compares the step with the model's own wire time (642 us snapshot, 828 us selector write). The base provider fails it once flags set at sub-microsecond times (712 us and 920 us); the head passes (685 us and 883 us). With whole-microsecond flags, as before this change, the base gave 687 us and 885 us. The service check asserts the modeled snapshot times and selector-write step counts in its board-cost rows, except the snapshot time of the 380 ns row, a fit to the board median that is only printed. The mixed-cost rows keep a rejected calibration for comparison and derive no board bound; the component-mean row omits callback and service work. A bundle 6 host fixture (checks/board-bundles-apps-model.c) checks the 1,268 permille limit against each run's measured wire time, including counter-tick boundaries. In the focused model check, a first service-model attempt used an incorrect expected 779 us at the 386 ns poll row; the actual result is 781 us, and the corrected run selected only the board-cost rows (raw logs, commands and executables under ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/pmic-completion/).

Provider mutants that checks/a733-pmic.c fails: a status other than 0xf8 after STOP treated as a fault; the status wait removed; the control check for 0x40 removed; the admission deadline check removed; the per-phase deadline check removed; line control read after every STOP; line control not read after the final STOP.

Reproduction: in each tree, clang -std=c11 -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Iinclude -Ichecks checks/a733-pmic-cost.c drivers/power/a733_pmic.c drivers/power/a733_rail_leases.c drivers/clock/a733_clock_leases.c drivers/gpu/a733_gpu_resources.c drivers/pinctrl/a733_pins.c drivers/pinctrl/a733_pin_tables.c -o cost && ./cost --limits. The service check adds drivers/power/a733_power_domains.c, a733_pmic_consumer.c and drivers/gpu/a733_gpu_power.c to checks/power-domains-service.c. Build logs, check logs and comparison objects are under ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/pmic-access.

hypothesis: Every target that links the provider, native adapter or service builds from the head tree, and the host checks the change touches pass.

conditions.toolchain: project AArch64 toolchain through the session configure script

conclusion: All 23 affected targets link smaller, and the listed host checks pass on head.
narrative:
Images rebuilt from the head and base trees (image lists and digests in ~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/pmic-access/images.txt). narrative:
Rank 9 (apps/usb-returning, rank-9-usb-v4/) was rebuilt and rerun with its qualifying pass conditions on port 3-3 on 2026-10-24 and passed (record set5-r9-v6-usb/), independent of the selector-write run. The returning thermal image of rank 6 does not link the provider: its board-run ELF has no a733_pmic_ symbol, and each of its seven units compiled from the tree has the same instructions before and after the change. The returning ADC image (apps/thermal-returning/adc.c) links the provider and is not board-qualified. Bundle 7 (apps/board-bundles-power/bundle7.c) either runs from its existing freeze on the current provider or is refrozen only after the rebuilt bundle 6 passes. The spin change otherwise affects only images that run the power service: GPU, accelerator, GPU display, HDMI, the DisplayPort and G2D board image, and the integrated OS image built from it; none is board-qualified.

Plain-DATA placement. The frozen bundle 6 of run four linked the adapter with plain DATA stores and a trailing CNTR DSB; its windows timed that placement directly. It met bundle 6's pass conditions with the same 1,268-permille median limit and first-step allowance, and its snapshots, XADDR window and bus-idle reads match the DSB SY pair run. That qualifies the plain-DATA placement for snapshots only. The native USB image of rank 9 needs a rerun on the current adapter (DSB SY after DATA and CNTR) before it relies on it, and a DCDC3 selector write, under its own gate, covers the write of the selector byte.

Base monitor for that rerun. apps/usb-returning/build.py --base-monitor links the base image's monitor.c object: the central monitor object, compiled without the monitor's counter option, has instructions that no board run has executed since the interrupt-cleanup readbacks and the replaced status. The base's monitor, built with the counter option, ran as s7-bb2-run and inside every bundle 6 image since. The builder requires that object's SHA-256 to match the base bundle's equivalence record and the base run to have passed with that bundle's image. The counter option only sets the EL1 event-counter access registers before EL1 entry and adds no field to the monitor's result record, so the USB runner needs no change. checks/board-bundles-apps.py --usb gives each object of the rebuilt image the origin of the passed or set image it equals, apart from debug sections, and only the two USB application units are new.

conclusion: Method record; results are in records pmic-access-bb6-run1 to run4.
narrative:
Method of bundle 6, which snapshots DCDC2 and DCDC4 (32 client snapshots; with two supply verifications 34 snapshots, each normally one service step). Pass: median and first steps within their bounds; a measured byte within 110% of nine bit times; snapshot bytes unchanged (0xff9e); no fault. Re-spins are reported and do not gate. Step records count re-spins: control-register polls beyond the second of a flag phase or of a STOP wait; a STOP wait lasts until M_STP reads clear and the status register reads 0xf8.

1. Cost windows in the service task at the park (the provider task, after the adapter's enter(), provider idle) on the provider's core at its clock. The windows live in apps/board-bundles-power/power.c, which the tree rule allows to use the adapter's operations.
2. Windows, 256 iterations each in eight timed sub-windows of 32; each prints its total and its fastest and slowest sub-window: CNTR reads with a733_mmio_read32_dsb_sy_both; plain CNTR reads whose value is discarded (issue throughput); plain CNTR reads where each value forms the next read's address (latency); time reads through the adapter's now; the adapter's read operation; a733_task_context_owner_el1() with IRQs unmasked as the earlier adapter called it, and the scheduler ticks inside that window; bb_twi_observe() on a scratch record as a flag poll that reads the flag clear (the trace observer run on every access).
3. Writes are timed inside the snapshots' own transfers: the pmic_write wrapper stamps the counter around the adapter's write, sums the ticks and keeps the fastest and slowest write, with no extra bus write. Those two stamps and the observer call per write, about 60 per snapshot, are inside the run's step times and limit direct comparison with the base 917 us median.
4. Wire time, once, with IRQs masked from before a byte-phase CNTR write: bb_status_spin() reads CNTR back to back until INT_FLAG (bit 3) reads set. The record keeps the stamp of the last read with the flag clear and of the first with it set, both from the write's return; the byte is the lower one. That step is excluded from the step statistics and counted as excluded.
5. Windows added in the eighth prepared set, three at the park and one during the snapshots, each 256 iterations in eight sub-windows of 32, IRQs masked unless stated: (a) counter overhead, the window loop with no body and a DSB SY at the end of each sub-window; (b) plain writes: 256 plain writes of the extended slave address register XADDR (S_TWI0 +0x04, 0x07083004) with the value it read, one DSB SY after each sub-window before its end stamp. A733 User Manual V1.00 section 18.11.10.2 with 18.11.10.1 (printed pages 1498 and 1499) gives XADDR one use, the second byte of a 10-bit slave address, compared only after the first byte matched 11110b and ADDR bits 2:1. Section 18.11.10.4 (pages 1499 to 1501) states the controller does not respond as a slave unless CNTR.A_ACK is set, which the provider never writes. A START or STOP needs M_STA or M_STP, INT_FLAG is a CNTR bit, and the pins follow the line-control register LCR (section 18.11.10.9, pages 1505 and 1506; SDA control enable, bit 0, on page 1506). An XADDR write therefore starts no bus phase, acknowledges no flag and drives no line. The window runs only when ADDR bits 7:3 are not 11110b, CNTR reads 0x40, STAT reads 0xf8 and LCR reads both lines high with neither forced (bb_xaddr_admitted() in apps/board-bundles-power/trace.c). Afterwards XADDR, ADDR, CNTR, STAT and LCR must each read the value read before the window or the image fails without a controlled outcome; a refused precondition skips the window and is recorded. (c) service loop between polls: the work query, the time read and the work query with the spin time, as pmic() in drivers/power/a733_power_domains.c runs them. (d) whole provider poll with the flag clear: up to four of the last four client snapshots carry this window and it stops at 256 samples, normally after the first; the service polls a queued snapshot back to back, without its spin, and stamps each a733_pmic_poll(). A poll that read only CNTR in a flag phase, wrote nothing, completed no phase and returned PENDING is a whole poll with the flag clear (entry, the provider object's try-lock, the time read and the flag read). IRQs stay unmasked as in the service; a sample with a scheduler tick inside is left out and counted. 256 samples are grouped into eight sub-windows of 32; 256 samples of the stamp pair alone give the per-sample overhead. Those snapshots leave the step records: of the 34 snapshots the wire-time spin step is excluded and the poll window takes one, so the summary normally reads STEPS recorded=32 and excluded=1; each further snapshot the window takes lowers the recorded count by one.
6. Completing polls in the recorded steps, a diagnostic option: checks/board-bundles-apps.py --complete-window compiles bundle 6 with BB6_COMPLETE_WINDOW=1; the default image omits the window. The window's stamp lengthened each snapshot step by about 12 us in the third and fourth runs. With the window, the wrapper of the poll's task check stamps the counter at the entry of every a733_pmic_poll() (one counter read per poll, inside the step times). A poll that completes a bus phase (a flag or a STOP wait, as the trace observer counts them) ends its span at the stamp after its first phase-start CNTR write returns. The spans of a recorded step join five records by that write: a byte whose poll wrote DATA first (0x48 for an address or register index), a receive (0x48 with no DATA write in the poll), a repeated START, a START after a STOP wait, and a STOP (0x58). Each record keeps the count, the summed ticks and the fastest and slowest span, printed as TWI_COMPLETE lines. The step that holds the wire-time spin and the poll window's snapshot are left out.

Conditions of the runs: one service core, trace observer and write stamps enabled, interrupts unmasked during ordinary steps. Production images omit that instrumentation and their step times were not measured.
